prompt: An e-reader app should read books aloud in a natural voice.
why: Speech synthesis turns text into audio.

prompt: A phone menu's prompts change weekly, and recording a voice actor each time is too slow.
tells: recording a voice actor each time is too slow
why: Generate the audio from text with text to speech.

prompt: The app needs to slow down and add a pause before reading account numbers aloud.
why: SSML controls rate, pauses and pronunciation in speech synthesis.
trap: This shapes generated speech, not recognized speech.

prompt: Visually impaired users want the app's notifications spoken out loud.
why: Speaking text aloud is text to speech.
trap: Inclusiveness is the principle; text to speech is the feature.

prompt: A bank wants its phone assistant to speak in a consistent voice that matches its brand.
why: Speech synthesis with a chosen or custom neural voice.
trap: A system prompt shapes words, not the sound of the voice.

prompt: The navigation app mispronounces local street names when reading directions aloud.
why: Fix pronunciation in speech synthesis with SSML or a custom lexicon.
trap: It's the output voice that's wrong, not what was heard.

prompt: A publisher wants audio versions of its back catalog without hiring narrators.
why: Generating speech from text is speech synthesis.

prompt: An airline's announcements must be spoken in English, Spanish and French from one written script.
tells: spoken in English, Spanish and French from one written script
why: Translate the script, then speak it with text to speech.
